speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities; to help identify the cause, have you been exposed to any new soaps, detergents, or fabrics recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you have denied new exposures and the rash has persisted for five months without complete resolution, does it show any specific pattern like symmetry, involvement of flexural areas, or changes with temperature? Also, have you noticed any scaling, crusting, or blisters on the lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Urticaria.
The history of a pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities persisting for five months without a specific trigger, combined with the absence of fever, joint pain, or scaling, is most consistent with chronic urticaria.
